items.title: Xinhua Middle East news summary at 2200 GMT, Nov. 18
text: JERUSALEM/GAZA -- Israeli security forces said Wednesday that they had launched a ground operation in central Gaza, advancing west of the ceasefire's "Yellow Line" and ordering hundreds of Palestinian families to leave their homes near two refugee camps.

The operation near the Nuseirat and Bureij refugee camps is aimed at dismantling underground militant infrastructure west of the "Yellow Line," the Israeli military and Shin Bet domestic security agency said in a joint statement, adding that it poses a "threat" to Israeli troops. (Israel-Gaza-Yellow Line)

BEIRUT -- A total of 84 Syrian refugees returned from Lebanon to Syria on Wednesday through the recently reopened Abboudiyeh-Daboussiyeh border crossing in the first organized voluntary return movement through the crossing since its reopening, the Delegation of the European Union to Lebanon said.

According to a press release on the delegation's website, EU Ambassador to Lebanon Sandra De Waele said the program provides counselling, documentation, transportation and allowances to refugees leaving Lebanon and settling back in Syria, while helping Lebanese authorities improve border procedures. (Lebanon-Syria-Refugees)

ALGIERS -- Eight people were killed in a road accident late Tuesday involving two heavy trucks and a motorcycle in Tamanrasset Province, southern Algeria, the Civil Protection authorities said Wednesday.
The accident occurred on the road linking Tazrouk and Ideles, about 110 km from Tazrouk locality, and was followed by a fire, according to the authorities. (Algeria-Road Accident-Deaths)

ANTALYA, Türkiye -- A Russian passenger plane carrying 65 passengers and four crew members landed safely at Antalya Airport in southern Türkiye on Wednesday following a bomb threat, local media reported.

The aircraft, a Sukhoi Superjet 100 operated by Russia's Azimuth Airlines on a flight from Mineralnye Vody, Russia, to Antalya, was placed under close monitoring after the threat was received, the Demiroren News Agency reported. (Türkiye-Plane-Bomb Threat)  ■

items.title: Xinhua Asia-Pacific news summary at 1600 GMT, Nov. 18
text: ULAN BATOR -- The Standing Committee on State Structure of Mongolia's parliament, or State Great Khural, on Wednesday endorsed President Ukhnaa Khurelsukh's request to resign from office.
Khurelsukh announced on Tuesday that he intended to step down in an effort to restore his reputation following allegations of abuse of power and corruption. (Mongolia-President-Resignation)

KUALA LUMPUR -- Malaysia's economy grew by 5.5 percent year on year in the third quarter of 2026, slowing from 6 percent in the previous quarter, as stronger exports and resilient domestic demand supported growth, the country's central bank said on Wednesday.

Bank Negara Malaysia (BNM) said in a statement that export growth strengthened, driven by technology-related shipments across electrical and electronics (E&E) and non-E&E products. (Malaysia-Economy-Data)

KABUL -- Afghanistan's economy is expected to expand by 3 percent in 2026, driven almost entirely by a robust agricultural harvest, according to the World Bank's latest Afghanistan Development Update.

However, output per person is projected to fall by 3.3 percent, its third consecutive annual decline, as the population is forecast to grow by 6.6 percent, according to the report issued by the World Bank on Wednesday. (Afghanistan-Economy-World Bank)

SINGAPORE -- Singapore will strengthen regional cooperation on climate action when it assumes the ASEAN chairmanship in 2027, with a focus on cross-border electricity trade, climate resilience and food security, Minister for Sustainability and the Environment Grace Fu said, according to a ministry statement on Tuesday.

Singapore will work with ASEAN partners to advance the ASEAN Power Grid and address challenges related to financing and implementing cross-border electricity projects, Fu said in Singapore's national statement at the 31st Conference of the Parties to the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change in Türkiye. (Singapore-ASEAN-Climate)  ■

JERUSALEM -- Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz said on Wednesday the military was prepared to seize more territory in Lebanon, Syria and Gaza, evacuate residents and turn captured areas into permanent security zones if fighting "flared up again."

"In the event of an escalation on these fronts, the IDF (Israel Defense Forces) is prepared to maneuver and capture additional territory," Katz said, adding that residents would be "evacuated" and "terrorist infrastructure" destroyed. (Israel-Military-Territory)
TEHRAN -- Iran's army said Wednesday that its combat drones targeted U.S. air defense systems as well as drone and missile launch platforms at Ali Al-Salem Air Base in Kuwait.

In a statement, the army's public relations office said its attack drones targeted Patriot air defense systems and platforms used to launch drones and missiles at the U.S. military base early Wednesday. (Iran-Kuwait-Drone Attack)

Prime Minister Sitiveni Rabuka said Wednesday the cabinet approved the declaration following advice from the National Disaster Risk Management Council, after assessments confirmed that crisis thresholds under the National El Nino Preparedness and Response Plan had reached. (Fiji-El Nino-Water Shortages)  ■

items.title: Xinhua Middle East news summary at 2200 GMT, Nov. 17
text: TEHRAN -- An Iranian provincial official said Tuesday that U.S. strikes on several areas of Qeshm Island caused no significant damage to residential or commercial areas or infrastructure, Iran's official news agency IRNA reported.

Ahmad Nafisi, Hormozgan province's deputy governor for political and security affairs, said the situation on Qeshm Island was under control, adding that all emergency response, service and administrative agencies were on full alert. (Iran-US-Qeshm Island)

JERUSALEM -- Israel said on Tuesday it would take countermeasures against Britain and consider ways to strengthen settlements in the occupied West Bank, after London imposed sanctions on eight companies involved in settlement expansion and on Tzav 9, an Israeli activist group accused of blocking aid to Gaza.

Calling the sanctions a "hostile act" targeting "private, law-abiding companies," Israel's Foreign Minister Gideon Sa'ar said Israel would not change its policies under external pressure and would consider new ways to strengthen Jewish communities in the West Bank. (Israel-Britain-Sanctions)

SANAA -- Yemen's Houthi group said Tuesday it had seized 10 districts across two provinces in a major offensive against government forces supported by the Saudi-led coalition, while threatening further attacks on Saudi oil facilities and airports.

In a televised statement broadcast by Houthi-run al-Masirah TV, Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Sarea said the operation had secured 10 districts covering around 7,100 square kilometers across the southwestern province of Taiz and the neighboring province of Lahj, following weeks of fierce fighting near the strategic Bab al-Mandab Strait. (Yemen-Houthis-Fighting)

MUSCAT -- Oman's Maritime Security Center said Tuesday that it had coordinated the evacuation of 24 crew members from a Panama-flagged tanker after a fire broke out aboard the vessel two nautical miles off the coast of Musandam Governorate.

The crew from the tanker TARA GAS was evacuated in cooperation with the Royal Navy of Oman and the Coast Guard Police of the Royal Oman Police, the center said in a statement. (Oman-Tanker-Evacuation)  ■

items.title: Full text: China-Russia-U.S. Heads of State Declaration toward Peace
text: SHENZHEN, Nov. 19 (Xinhua) -- The following is the full text of the China-Russia-U.S. Heads of State Declaration toward Peace, released on Thursday.
China-Russia-U.S. Heads of State Declaration toward Peace

Xi Jinping, President of the People's Republic of China, Vladimir Putin, President of the Russian Federation, and Donald J. Trump, President of the United States of America, met in Shenzhen on November 19, 2026. The Russian and U.S. heads of state expressed appreciation to China for hosting this historic trilateral Summit. The three heads of state had an in-depth exchange of views on the current international situation and committed to maintaining strategic stability and international security.

1. As permanent members of the United Nations Security Council, China, Russia, and the United States committed to reform the U.N. so that the U.N. can respond more effectively to global challenges and conform to its fundamental mission of international peace and security.
2. The three countries plan to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products for the benefit of all nations. They reaffirmed the importance of stable energy flows.

3. The three heads of state recognized that the principle of state consent and respect for immunities of State officials are of paramount importance, and concurred that the International Criminal Court and other similar bodies must not abuse their jurisdiction.

4. The three heads of state reaffirmed that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought. The three countries will conduct a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons.

items.title: Foreign journalists praise Shenzhen's remarkable transformation
text: "A city of wonders," "the Silicon Valley of China" and "a really incredible city" -- foreign journalists attending the 2026 APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting have expressed admiration for Shenzhen's remarkable transformation.
"It has grown so much in just four decades, and the transformation has been amazing," said Reginald Ritesh Chandar, a journalist from Fiji.
From rapid urban development to advances in artificial intelligence and robotics, Shenzhen's achievements offer a vivid example of China's reform and opening up and innovation-driven development.
Their impressions highlight not only Shenzhen's transformation into a global innovation hub, but also the dynamism and vitality of China's development.

items.title: Foreign journalists highlight APEC's role in advancing cooperation
Chinese friendship association president visits Nepal
text: KATHMANDU, Nov. 19 (Xinhua) -- Yang Wanming, president of the Chinese People's Association for Friendship with Foreign Countries (CPAFFC), led a delegation on a visit to Nepal from Tuesday to Thursday, focusing on consolidating China-Nepal traditional friendship and advancing bilateral cooperation across diverse fields.

During the visit, Yang held separate meetings with senior Nepali officials, including Speaker of the House of Representatives Dol Prasad Aryal, Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal, and Sunita Dangol, acting mayor of Kathmandu Metropolitan City.
The Chinese delegation also attended a collective symposium with prominent Nepali friendly personages.

Yang extended sincere condolences to Nepal over the severe mudslide disaster that hit the China-Nepal border on Aug. 26 this year. He stressed that the CPAFFC is willing to assist within its capacity to support Nepal's post-disaster reconstruction.

Both sides affirmed their commitment to implement the consensus reached by the leaders of China and Nepal, and reiterated adherence to the positioning of the strategic partnership of cooperation featuring ever-lasting friendship for development and prosperity.

Both sides agreed to further deepen friendly exchanges and cooperation in local governance, parliamentary communication, people-to-people ties, economy and trade, culture, tourism and youth exchanges.

items.title: Submarine steams towards the sea
Prologis vice chairman: Asia-Pacific to remain world's biggest growth engine
text: Shane Tedjarati, vice chairman of Prologis, said openness, transparency and collaboration are key to the Asia-Pacific region's growth and to China-U.S. relations, adding that he hopes for more dialogue between the two countries.
"The more we talk, the more we understand each other, the better it is," he said.
The business executive made the remarks in an interview with People's Daily Online after the APEC CEO Summit 2026's morning session in Shenzhen, south China's Guangdong Province, on Nov. 18.

"In the next 10 years, the Asia-Pacific will (remain) the biggest engine of growth for the world," Tedjarati said, adding that the region is very dynamic, with the largest economic and commercial market in the world, as well as the world's largest population.

For Prologis, he said, the more open, transparent and fluid trade and business interactions are, the better. "We are of course an American company, but we have footprints all over the world," he added.
Xu Jiayuan, as an intern, also contributed to this article.

items.title: Feature: Chinese folk melodies build cross-cultural bridge in Ethiopia
text: Chinese artists perform at the concert held under the theme "Golden Bell Resounds, Harmony Along the Silk Road" in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia, Nov. 17, 2026. Music and art enthusiasts gathered in Addis Ababa, the Ethiopian capital, on Tuesday night for a special cross-cultural concert featuring Chinese folk music and joint performances. (Xinhua/Liu Fangqiang)

ADDIS ABABA, Nov. 18 (Xinhua) -- Music and art enthusiasts gathered in Addis Ababa, the Ethiopian capital, on Tuesday night for a special cross-cultural concert featuring Chinese folk music and joint performances.

Held under the theme "Golden Bell Resounds, Harmony Along The Silk Road" at the Ashenafi Kebede Performing Arts Center at Addis Ababa University (AAU), the event was organized by the Beijing Federation of Literary and Art Circles, in partnership with the Chinese Embassy in Ethiopia, the Ethiopian Ministry of Culture and Tourism, and the AAU.

The concert brought together Chinese and Ethiopian artists, featuring performances by about 20 renowned musicians mainly from both the Central Conservatory of Music of China and the China Conservatory of Music.
The captivating performance included a diverse musical repertoire, blending traditional Chinese folk music with classical piano and creating a rich auditory experience for music and art enthusiasts.

Welcoming the art troupe on its performance tour in Ethiopia and Africa, Chinese Ambassador to Ethiopia Chen Hai highlighted the vital significance of the concert in fostering a greater understanding of the cultural and artistic values of both sides.

With 2026 designated as the China-Africa Year of People-to-People Exchanges, Chen noted that both sides have maintained frequent cultural exchanges during this commemorative year. He said the concert, featuring traditional folk music and cross-cultural performances, aims to further deepen and celebrate China-Ethiopia and China-Africa cultural exchanges as well as lasting people-to-people ties.

Noting that China and Ethiopia both possess long histories, splendid civilizations, and fine traditional cultures, Chen expressed confidence that the performance would connect artists from both nations, particularly younger generations, through music to maintain a dynamic dialogue between the two civilizations, forge stronger bonds, and continuously enrich their all-weather strategic partnership.

The concert began with a joint rendition performed by the Chinese art troupe, with Ethiopian artists playing the cello and double bass, drawing sustained applause from the audience. A total of 11 musical pieces were presented during the concert, which lasted for approximately two hours.

As 2026 also marks the milestone 70th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between China and African countries, participants highlighted the event's significant historical significance, as a range of cultural celebrations are taking place across the continent throughout the year.

items.title: India braces as Cyclone Akvan approaches east coast
text: NEW DELHI, Nov. 18 (Xinhua) -- Authorities in eastern India have stepped up disaster preparations as severe cyclonic storm Akvan moves north-northwestward over the Bay of Bengal and is forecast by the India Meteorological Department (IMD) to cross India's east coast by Friday noon.

The storm is expected to cross between Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh and Puri in Odisha, with maximum sustained winds of 90 to 100 kmph and gusts of up to 110 kmph. The IMD has advised fishermen not to venture into the southwest, west-central and northwest Bay of Bengal until Friday.

In Odisha, authorities have deployed 74 rescue teams and identified more than 200,000 people for possible evacuation. Schools, colleges and courtyard shelters run under the Integrated Child Development Services programme in Malkangiri district will be closed on Nov. 19 and 20.
In neighboring Andhra Pradesh, fishing operations have been suspended, while 13 National Disaster Response Force teams and 11 State Disaster Response Force teams have been placed on standby.

items.title: China-Russia-US summit positive, constructive, fruitful: Xi
text: SHENZHEN -- President Xi Jinping on Thursday said that the China-Russia-US summit has been positive, constructive and fruitful.
Xi made the remarks while summarizing the main consensus reached at the summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and US President Donald Trump in Shenzhen, South China's Guangdong province.
The three countries share the same view on safeguarding world peace, and all stressed that the hard-won peace must be cherished, Xi said.
They all agree that major countries should take the legitimate security concerns of every country seriously and that dialogue and negotiation are the right choice to resolve differences, Xi said.
"There is hope for peace as long as dialogue does not cease and the door does not close," Xi said.
They also agreed that cooperation is essential to overcoming challenges, Xi said.
The three countries should follow through on the consensus reached at the summit, continue to strengthen communication, promote peace through cooperation, and work together to build a better world.

items.title: Farmers in Hebei's Taihang Mountains carry out winter terrace maintenance
text: Farmers in the Taihang Mountains of Shexian county in Handan, Hebei province, are using the brief window before the soil freezes to carry out winter maintenance on the region's terraced fields.

In Wangjinzhuang village, the core area of the Shexian Dryland Stone Terraced System, farmers have been busy plowing land, leveling plots, repairing stone retaining walls, and gathering crop residue. The work is aimed at conserving soil moisture before the ground hardens, part of preparations for next year's spring sowing, according to locals.

The system was recognized by the UN Food and Agriculture Organization as a Globally Important Agricultural Heritage System in May 2022. The terraces date back to Yuan Dynasty (1271-1368) and rely on stone ridges and soil cover to make farming possible in a limestone landscape short of fertile soil and rain.
Across the wider system, terraced land covers nearly 2,800 hectares across 46 villages. In the Wangjinzhuang core zone alone, 800 hectares is divided into more than 80,000 small plots.

items.title: Starbucks China rolls out in-store baking to over 100 locations
text: Starbucks China has introduced in-store baking at more than 100 stores in over 30 cities after food sales nearly doubled at some locations that tested the program, the company said on Thursday.

The rollout will test whether freshly baked pastries can persuade more customers to buy food with their drinks and spend more per visit. Starbucks began testing the program at nearly 10 stores in September 2025. It did not disclose average food sales growth across the pilot stores.
The initial lineup includes 11 items for breakfast and afternoon tea. Suppliers prepare the dough and ship it frozen to stores, where employees bake the pastries and put them on sale the same day.

Starbucks worked with suppliers to refine dough recipes, fermentation, and cold-chain logistics. Participating stores installed commercial ovens imported from Italy and dedicated freezers, and employees received baking training. Starbucks said the model allows it to test new products more quickly and bring successful items to stores nationwide in about six months.

The launch follows Starbucks China's announcement that it would invest more than 300 million yuan to improve in-store service. In April, Starbucks completed a deal with Boyu Capital to form a joint venture for its China retail business.

Boyu holds a 60 percent stake in the venture, while Starbucks retains 40 percent and continues to license its brand. Nearly 8,000 previously company-operated stores on the Chinese mainland shifted to a franchise model under the deal. The partners aim to expand the network to 20,000 stores over the long term.

items.title: Nvidia shifts its stance on chip exports
text: US semiconductor firm Nvidia has confirmed it will halt shipping H200 chips to China, with fourth-quarter guidance excluding all Hopper GPU architecture data-center revenue previously authorized under US approval, interim CEO Colette Kress said on Wednesday.

The policy shift follows a dramatic leadership change. On Nov 12, the board announced that co-founder Jensen Huang had stepped down as president, CEO and director effective immediately, with chief financial officer Kress appointed interim chief executive.

Huang had been the strongest advocate for restoring chip exports to China, having negotiated an arrangement under which H200 shipments passed through the United States are subject to 25 percent tariffs paid to the US Treasury.
Even under that framework, Nvidia still sold $2.4 billion of H200 products to China in the third quarter — but now the revenue for the fourth quarter is guided to zero, the company said.

Roger Sheng, vice-president of US market research firm Gartner, said Huang was the pivotal figure linking demand-side financing to supply-side execution. "Without him, Asian suppliers and buyers of Nvidia's products — including Chinese companies — will inevitably be affected," Sheng said.
Sheng said the leadership vacuum at Nvidia has emboldened hardline voices in Washington to push for tighter artificial intelligence curbs.

The US government said on Monday that it was tightening what it alleged was a "loophole" that has allowed Chinese tech firms to bypass US restrictions on accessing the most advanced AI chips through third countries. The new rule, released by the US Department of Commerce, will require buyers of advanced semiconductors from certain countries to secure a license before selling or transferring such chips.

Investment bank Jefferies estimates the move could cut Nvidia's data-center revenue by $44 billion to $62 billion next year, though Kress said ample backlog for next-generation products, such as the company's Vera Rubin NVL72 — a rack-scale AI supercomputer — will cushion the near-term blow.

Nvidia also announced the establishment of a board-level national security committee to oversee export-control compliance and global trade risks, with the compliance team reporting both to the committee and the interim CEO.
Analysts said the moves signal a strategic pivot from a founder-driven, pragmatic approach vis-a-vis China, to a more cautious, compliance-first posture.

items.title: Hong Kong well-placed to power APEC shipping sector's growth
text: With the global trade landscape growing more diversified and complex, Hong Kong is well positioned to leverage its strengths in maritime services, financing and a broad range of professional services to support development of the regional shipping sector, enhance supply-chain resilience, and forge coordination across the Asia-Pacific region, industry experts said.

"For Hong Kong, the opportunity lies in serving this increasingly demanding trading environment through both its port and wider maritime services," said Sandy Chan, managing director of the Hong Kong Shipowners Association.

Global shipping routes have changed dramatically in recent years as companies adapt to evolving trade relationships between economies and disruptions at major maritime choke points, with many businesses reassessing where they manufacture, source materials and store inventories. These shifts often result in longer voyages and higher costs, placing additional strain on supply-chain reliability.
Chan said these changes have underscored the importance of connections between manufacturing hubs, regional suppliers and end markets across the Asia-Pacific region.

They have also increased demand for more comprehensive supporting services, infrastructure and expertise, as well as stronger safety capabilities, efficient customs clearance, digital connectivity and coordination between ports.
Against this backdrop, she said Hong Kong's port and maritime service sector can benefit from opportunities arising from the increasingly connected regional port network.

At the same time, the city can draw on its distinctive advantages — from shipping insurance, ship management and maritime arbitration, to financing and other professional services — to help businesses in the region manage supply-chain risks, diversify transport routes and maintain trade continuity.

Currently, there are more than 300 shipping agents and managers, as well as overseas shipping companies' representative offices in Hong Kong. As of June, loans and advances in the shipping sector amounted to approximately HK$105 billion ($13.38 billion), with six of the world's top ten book-runners for shipping syndicated loans maintaining offices here, according to Hong Kong Maritime and Port Development Board.
In 2025, five insurers launched a marine specialty risk pool in the city, which covers war and related risks for Hong Kong and Chinese mainland shipowners.
The pool now includes more than 1,000 vessels.

Mike Lai Kee-hung, chair professor of shipping and logistics at the Hong Kong Polytechnic University's Business School, said Hong Kong can aid Asia-Pacific businesses by serving as a "regional resilience platform" which combines alternative transport arrangements with financing, insurance, reliable information and legal support.

"It is not necessary to route every shipment through Hong Kong, but to ensure that businesses can continue trading when their usual routes, suppliers or payment arrangements become disrupted," Lai said.

items.title: China Proposes Tougher Rules to Curb Skills Certification Fraud
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019293/China Proposes Tougher Rules to Curb Skills Certification Fraud
text: China has proposed its first regulation on vocational skills certifications, cracking down on fraudulent credentials and tightening oversight of certification bodies.
The Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security released the draft regulation on Nov. 12, with public feedback open until Dec. 12. No date has been set for when the rules will take effect.

China now has more than 220 million skilled workers — including electricians, AI trainers, and elderly-care workers — accounting for about 30% of its workforce, according to the ministry. Vocational skills certificates can bring benefits such as cash subsidies, children’s school enrollment, and fast-tracked residency applications.
Fraudulent vocational skills certificates have proliferated online in recent years, prompting a nationwide crackdown on bogus credentials in 2022.

The proposed regulation would tighten oversight of certification bodies, barring them from making misleading claims or leaking exam questions. In addition, certificates can be issued only to candidates who pass the required assessments, rather than those who simply pay to obtain them.

The draft also outlines that organizations responsible for vocational qualification assessments would be barred from offering related training. Institutions that issue certificates without first registering with the government, as well as those that forge, alter, or trade certificates, may face suspension, confiscation of illegal earnings, and fines of 10,000 to 100,000 yuan ($1,500 to $15,000).

The rules also outline penalties for examiners who engage in misconduct, candidates who cheat, and officials who fail to perform their duties properly. Employers will be encouraged to use workers’ certified skill levels as a key factor in determining pay.

Previously, workers obtained vocational qualifications through government-organized exams. Starting in 2020, however, China phased out most government-issued vocational qualifications, shifting responsibility to registered and supervised third-party organizations. By the end of 2025, 32,000 such organizations were in operation nationwide.

Cheng Xiezhong, a law professor at the China University of Political Science and Law, told domestic media that the shift had “helped expand the pool of skilled workers” but had also led to uneven standards among certification bodies and a widespread increase in bogus certificates.

An investigation by domestic media this June found vocational certificates openly advertised on multiple Chinese e-commerce platforms. In one case, a reporter paid just 300 yuan for a mechanical equipment installer certificate showing passing scores on tests they had never taken.

Previous reports also found that some training providers issued course completion certificates rather than recognized vocational credentials. Others lured young jobseekers into “training loan” scams, persuading them to borrow thousands of yuan for courses.

items.title: Bot, Interrupted: DeepSeek Users Report New Limits on Free Chats
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019284/Bot, Interrupted: DeepSeek Users Report New Limits on Free Chats
text: Chinese AI model DeepSeek has reportedly begun limiting use of its free chatbot by reducing the number of characters users can input and discontinuing inactive conversations after seven days.

DeepSeek users began reporting seeing an error message — “Due to server overload, the use limit has been reached” — on Monday when they tried to continue chats inactive for a week or when they tried to input larger volumes of text, according to posts on microblogging platform Weibo.

According to domestic media, users of the large language model (LLM) can now only enter around 40,000 characters at a time (a page of Chinese text typically ranges from 500 to 800 characters). Previously, the chatbot had no publicly stated text limit. Once users reach their daily limit, DeepSeek displays an error message.
It is reportedly the first time DeepSeek, headquartered in China’s eastern city of Hangzhou, has restricted free-user access since its launch in January 2025.

According to its official status page, DeepSeek has experienced 57 outages or performance degradations this year, without providing additional explanation. Domestic media reported that disruptions in the first half of the year mainly involved slower responses, delays in data generation, and occasional request failures. After October, prolonged global outages began to occur more frequently.

Usage caps apply only to individual users, but because DeepSeek has no related paid plan, those who hit their capacity cannot pay for more. App developers, who pay to use DeepSeek through an application programming interface, or API, a connection that shares data between their software and the AI model, are subject to separate limits and per-use billing.

As of Wednesday, DeepSeek had not announced a reason for the new rules or whether it might lift them. Developers who spotted references to a “Coding Plan” in the website’s code have speculated that the company may soon implement a paid subscription plan for individual users.

Online, users debated the new limits, with many expressing outrage and complaining that the company had not rolled out a paid plan option for individual users before the usage limit. “I feel like I’m a widow who just lost her husband,” wrote one user on lifestyle platform Xiaohongshu, also known as RedNote.

Others sympathized with DeepSeek, arguing that data is costly or hypothesizing that the company was clamping down on users developing companion relationships with its AI, alluding to China’s ban on AI products designed to mimic human personalities that took effect on July 15.

Data from OpenRouter, a U.S.-based platform that provides access to numerous AI models through one interface, showed DeepSeek’s latest model processing 59.2 trillion tokens the week of Nov. 9 to 15, topping OpenRouter’s weekly token usage chart.

Long chats are more costly for LLM developers because models must parse more information with each reply. Industry watchers told domestic media that the higher costs mean DeepSeek may now have to choose between training new models, serving paying API customers, and providing free chats.

items.title: Lu Xun’s Overlooked Translations That Shaped Modern Chinese Literature
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019257/Lu Xun’s Overlooked Translations That Shaped Modern Chinese Literature
text: In 1903, 22-year-old Lu Xun, then a student in Japan, wandered into a bookstore in Jimbocho, Tokyo’s famed book district, where his attention was caught by a science fiction novel titled “A Journey to the Moon in Ninety-Seven Hours and Twenty Minutes.” Translated into Japanese by Inoue Tsutomu and believed to have been written by an American author, the novel appealed to Lu Xun’s own ambition to popularize scientific knowledge in China, where modern science education was still in its infancy. Enthusiastic about the genre’s potential, he quickly set about translating it into Chinese.

His version, “Yuejie Lüxing” (“A Journey to the Moon”), published the same year and among the earliest Chinese translations of science fiction, marked the beginning of his prolific career as a translator, long before he became celebrated as the “founding father of modern Chinese literature” for his novels and essays.

Today, we know that Inoue had misidentified the original author. The novel was, in fact, Jules Verne’s “De la Terre à la Lune: trajet direct en 97 heures 20 minutes,” published in 1865 and widely translated into English in the 1870s. Misled by its setting — in post-Civil War America, where members of the Baltimore Gun Club plan to fire a projectile at the moon — Inoue assumed the author was American. Lu Xun, following this assumption, opened his translation with original passages describing America in extravagant detail to provide context for his Chinese readers.

The curious story of this translation and mistranslation of Verne’s novel illuminates how literary forms and ideas traveled across borders at the turn of the 20th century, particularly in East Asia following the First Sino-Japanese War (1894–1895), when waves of Chinese students — including Lu Xun — went to study in Japan.

It was in Tokyo, amid the intellectual riches of Jimbocho, where he spent much of his leisure time, that Lu Xun was drawn to translation. Japan’s Meiji Restoration, which restored imperial rule in 1868, had already spurred a flood of translations from European languages into Japanese. Eager to take advantage of this wealth of material, Lu Xun, by then proficient in Japanese, with a working knowledge of German and some Russian, immersed himself in these texts. On one hand, he translated texts from cultures he perceived as more scientifically and technologically advanced, with the aim of promoting science education among his own people; on the other hand, he gradually developed an interest in writers from marginalized communities and nations, believing their experiences would resonate with China, which had endured decades of foreign invasion and exploitation. Later, recounting his decision to translate the exiled Russian writer and activist Vasily Eroshenko, he made clear that he saw translation not simply as an aesthetic pursuit, but as a means of giving voice to the oppressed.
[continua sulla fonte originale]

items.title: Lesson in Endurance: China’s Schools Start Later to Ease Burden on Students
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019288/Lesson in Endurance: China’s Schools Start Later to Ease Burden on Students
text: Parents across China have for years raised concerns about how long children spend in school each day, with some high school students logging at least 15 hours in class.
In recent weeks, education authorities nationwide have been pushing back start times for all grades to ease the burden.

Schools in Nanjing, capital of the eastern Jiangsu province, reportedly began introducing changes in November. A parent told the Yangtze Evening Post that their child, a high school freshman, now starts studying at 7:15 a.m. and finishes after-school study sessions at 9:20 p.m., a 45-minute reduction from the previous schedule of 6:40 a.m. to 9:30 p.m.

Jiangyin, a city about two hours east by road, also announced across-the-board adjustments on Nov. 5. Classes now start at 8 a.m. at primary schools, 7:40 a.m. at middle schools, and 7:20 a.m. at high schools.

During an edition of the show “Zhengfeng Hotline” broadcast live on Jiangsu TV on Oct. 27, Jiang Yong, director of the provincial education department, said, “The issue of excessively long school hours is severe. As the education authority, we feel a profound sense of remorse.”

According to the 2022 China Family Panel Studies (CFPS), a nationally representative longitudinal survey of families, individuals, and communities conducted by researchers at Peking University, 46% of full-time high school students study for more than 12 hours on a typical weekday, while for nearly 25% it’s over 14 hours. Including weekdays and rest days, high school students average 68.6 hours of study time per week.

For a 2026 article published in Youth Studies, researchers from Renmin University of China and Peking University analyzed survey data relating to students aged 6 to 17. They found that high school students spend on average 10 hours and 54 minutes engaged in education-related activities on weekdays and six hours and 29 minutes on weekends. That adds up to about 67.5 hours.
These activities cover in-class instruction, after-class study, off-campus tutoring, and commuting to and from school.
However, for some, 67.5 hours is merely a baseline. The study reveals a direct correlation between a parent’s education level and how long their child spends studying.

For those with only a middle school education or lower, their children study an average of eight hours and two minutes a day. If the parent holds a high school diploma or a university degree, that time rises by 15 or 29 minutes, respectively.
Study time also varies by location and school quality.

The CFPS shows that high school students in China’s four municipalities — Beijing, Shanghai, Tianjin, and Chongqing — as well as provincial capitals study 73.5 hours a week, nearly five hours more than the national average. Meanwhile, for students at key schools, which receive preferential funding and attract high-quality teachers, the figure rises to 75.1 hours.
Both comparisons suggest students in urban high schools and top-tier institutions endure a heavier academic burden.

items.title: China’s Basic Insurance to Cover CAR T-Cell Cancer Therapy
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019275/China’s Basic Insurance to Cover CAR T-Cell Cancer Therapy
text: China will include a CAR T-cell therapy in its national health insurance scheme for the first time, making a blood cancer treatment that once cost over 1 million yuan ($150,000) per dose more accessible.

The National Healthcare Security Administration announced on Nov. 14 that relmacabtagene autoleucel, or relma-cel, made by Shanghai-based biotech firm JW Therapeutics and sold under the brand name Carteyva, will be covered by insurance starting Jan. 1. The therapy has three approved uses for different types of lymphoma and costs 1.29 million yuan per dose.

CAR T-cell therapy is primarily used to treat types of lymphoma and involves extracting and genetically modifying a patient’s own immune cells to target cancer cells, before infusing them back into the body. China approved its first CAR T-cell therapy product in 2021.

Most of China’s population is covered by the country’s national insurance scheme: 1.33 billion were enrolled in basic medical insurance by the end of 2025. Only drugs listed in the national insurance catalog can be partially reimbursed through the medical insurance fund. For drugs not listed, patients must usually bear 100% of the cost.

For years, CAR T-cell drugs were excluded from the national insurance list because an unwritten industry rule held that drugs priced above 300,000 yuan rarely secured coverage, limiting patient access, according to Shanghai-based media outlet The Paper.

The rate of CAR T-cell drug use as a second-line treatment for large B-cell lymphoma in China is about one-sixth of that in the United States, while use as a third-line treatment is about one-10th of the rate in the U.S. and Europe.

Carteyva was one of five CAR T-cell therapies included last year in China’s first commercial insurance list for high-cost innovative drugs. This year, those drugs became eligible for national coverage. Two CAR T-cell drug manufacturers, including JW Therapeutics, entered insurance coverage negotiations on Sept. 6.
“Two or three years ago, we wouldn’t have dared to imagine this,” Tian Feng, JW Therapeutics chairman and CEO, told The Paper.
China records about 101,500 new lymphoma cases each year. Carteyva is available at more than 200 certified hospitals nationwide.

The updated national reimbursement list adds 107 drugs covering oncology, chronic diseases, mental illnesses, rare diseases, and pediatric medications. A separate commercial insurance list, which covers drugs outside the basic scheme, includes 12 new treatments.

“This is a historic moment for lymphoma patients in China,” Tian said, adding that when he and the company received the news, “everyone really felt that the treatment of lymphoma patients in China had entered a new, very exciting era.”

items.title: A Chinese Medical Drama’s Remedy for Big-City Blues: Go Home
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019269/A Chinese Medical Drama’s Remedy for Big-City Blues: Go Home
text: A TV drama about a doctor who returns to his small hometown after being fired from a prestigious city-based position has become a hit among young Chinese, who resonate with its message of finding purpose away from competitive urban areas.

“Small Town Remedy” has been hotly discussed since its Nov. 4 finale. Premiering Oct. 21, the show follows Liu Zhengliang, played by A-list actor Xiao Zhan, a young neurosurgeon who returns to his hometown in northeastern China — or Dongbei — from a major hospital following a botched surgery in which his patient dies.

The show’s popularity comes amid a broader shift in attitudes among young Chinese, who increasingly seek a more sustainable work-life balance and self-care amid growing fatigue stemming from relentless competition and conventional definitions of success.

Socially awkward and unfamiliar with local customs, Liu initially struggles to return to life at home after leaving his post in the southern metropolis of Shenzhen. The series depicts how his brother, childhood friends, and former hospital colleagues gradually help him overcome the trauma of his failed operation, among other personal struggles, such as the death of his mother.

Fans have reported being drawn to the drama’s lighthearted tone and the witty humor commonly associated with China’s Northeast, despite tackling heavy subject matter such as illness, death, and grief.

Its popularity has also sparked an online trend of learning the Dongbei dialect, with video lessons gaining traction on social media. One related hashtag — “‘Small Town Remedy’ Dongbei dialect listening test” — had amassed nearly 1.4 million views on microblogging platform Weibo as of Monday.

The 29-episode drama has earned an average rating of 8 out of 10 on review platform Douban and reached an audience of 148 million across all streaming platforms, according to data from domestic streaming platform iQiyi. Related hashtags on short-video platform Douyin, China’s version of TikTok, had also garnered more than 8 billion views.

Since the show’s finale, online users have been debating what Liu’s next move should be. Some suggest that as a talented young doctor, he should return to a major hospital to pursue better career prospects, while others say he’d be better off staying in his hometown, where he’d have the emotional space to continue recovering and potentially find greater purpose using his medical skills.

“Everyone wants to go to Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou, and Shenzhen, but if life away from home is too difficult, returning to your hometown is not a step backward, nor is it something to be ashamed of,” one user wrote beneath a post discussing the show on lifestyle platform Xiaohongshu, also known as RedNote. “One’s hometown can be a great choice, too.”

“As urbanization continues, more and more young people are facing the same dilemmas as Liu Zhengliang,” another Xiaohongshu user wrote in a comment under the same post, referring to Liu’s struggles with cultural identity and homesickness. “I think the theme of this show really suits the times.”
[continua sulla fonte originale]

items.title: Shanghai Sacks Two Scientists Over Child’s Death in Gene Trial
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019274/Shanghai Sacks Two Scientists Over Child’s Death in Gene Trial
text: Shanghai authorities have dismissed two researchers after an investigation into a child’s death following experimental gene-editing treatment found unheeded safety warnings, failures in ethical review, and undisclosed payments and gifts from the family.

The child had Snijders Blok-Campeau syndrome, a rare neurodevelopmental disorder with no effective treatment, according to findings released Friday by the Shanghai investigation team. The family contributed 5.3 million yuan ($800,000) toward the research and separately gave researchers approximately 1.06 million yuan in money and gifts.

In July 2023, the family approached Qiu Zilong, deputy director of Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine’s Songjiang Research Institute, hoping his team could develop a customized gene-editing treatment, investigators said.
The child received an injection at the university’s affiliated Xinhua Hospital on March 24, 2025, and died seven days later.
At an emergency review April 2, the hospital’s ethics committee attributed the death to thrombotic microangiopathy, a complication of gene therapy, and ordered the study terminated.

The death went unmentioned in related preclinical research Qiu’s team published in Nature in February 2026, investigators said. The team reported using gene editing to correct a single error in the DNA code of mouse brain cells, restoring levels of a protein essential for normal brain development. The researchers said tests in monkeys also suggested the technique’s potential for use in humans.

Five months later, a joint investigation by Science and Retraction Watch revealed the fatal human trial and reported that the Nature paper had also omitted evidence of liver and kidney damage in animal safety tests.
Shanghai authorities subsequently established a team to investigate the preclinical research, the hospital’s clinical study, and the data underlying the Nature paper.
Investigators found that Qiu’s team had failed to promptly share a safety report from experiments on nonhuman primates with the clinical study’s lead investigator, leaving warning signals unheeded.

Xinhua Hospital’s ethics committee approved the study despite insufficient toxicology and safety evidence, proceeding without additional material it had requested. The hospital also failed to independently and adequately assess the study’s scientific basis and safety.
Investigators said that although the consent form warned the family of serious complications and adverse events, it did not prominently communicate the risk of death.

Investigators found no data fabrication in the Nature paper but identified discrepancies between the research methods used and those described. Data from the same experimental batch had also been presented separately without explanation.

The Nature paper also failed to disclose financial conflicts involving four researchers. Qiu received expensive liquor and electronics worth approximately 100,000 yuan, while Xinhua Hospital associate researcher Yang Kan, the Nature paper’s first and corresponding author, received 900,000 yuan and expensive liquor. Two other members of Qiu’s team each received 30,000 yuan.

items.title: What Made Jade So Valuable in Ancient China and the Americas?
items.link: https://www.sixthtone.com/news/1019256/What Made Jade So Valuable in Ancient China and the Americas?
text: Recent exhibitions at the Shanghai Museum and Beijing’s Capital Museum have introduced Chinese audiences to the civilizations of the ancient Americas. For Chinese visitors, the importance placed on jade may feel familiar. In both ancient China and Mesoamerica, finely worked jade adorned the powerful and accompanied them into the grave, a striking similarity that has long attracted scholarly interest.

How did jade come to carry such authority? One way to explore this question is to compare the jade traditions of Liangzhu and the Classic Maya lowlands, two societies from ancient China and the Americas. Liangzhu was an early regional state near present-day Hangzhou, capital of eastern China’s Zhejiang province, around 3300–2300 BC, with a walled capital, an extensive system of dams, and a pronounced social hierarchy. In the Classic Maya lowlands, spanning parts of present-day Mexico, Guatemala, and Belize, cities ruled by royal dynasties flourished around AD 300–900. Both Liangzhu and Maya cities hold UNESCO World Heritage status.

Thousands of years separated the two societies, and there is no evidence of direct contact between them. Yet both had complex social hierarchies in which powerful ritual authorities played important roles. By tracing jade from the selection of raw stone to its final resting place, we can see how control over labor, knowledge, and materials helped establish its authority in ways that were both similar and distinct.

Jade was valued in both ancient China and the Americas long before Liangzhu and the Classic Maya. The concept of jade encompasses several kinds of stone. Liangzhu’s finest ritual jades were made from nephrite, while Maya jade was principally jadeite. Both were prized for their appearance and could be polished to a lustrous finish. Craftspeople shaped jade using abrasives such as sand mixed with water. Working with different stones helped them recognize differences in hardness and toughness and determine which materials were best suited to particular objects.

In Liangzhu, material choice was closely tied to the form and status of the finished artifact. Other stones, such as serpentine, were generally used for small, less prestigious ornaments. Among the Maya, by contrast, the symbolic meanings of stones were more closely associated with their colors. Green and blue-green evoked water, cultivating maize, and renewed life. Jadeite remained highly prized, but a wider range of similarly colored stones could also be valued for their quality and craftsmanship.
Not everyone had equal access to these raw materials or the specialized skills needed to work them. This inequality helped establish jade’s association with power.

Workshops within and immediately outside Liangzhu city made prestigious ritual objects from nephrite. A short distance away, a large workshop complex specialized in small serpentine ornaments. Despite their proximity, the workshops used different materials and produced different types of objects. The fine finish of these serpentine ornaments, however, shows that their makers were skilled.
[continua sulla fonte originale]

items.title: Press conference for AIE Expo 2026 held in Macao
text: The press conference for the 2026 Global Artificial Intelligence Manufacturing and Electronics Expo (AIE Expo 2026) was held in China's Macao Special Administrative Region (SAR) on November 13, bringing together technology companies from across the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA) to showcase their latest innovations.

Organizers also outlined the expo's preparations and plans for international cooperation. Wong Yee Lam, a member of the Commerce and Investment Promotion Institute of the Macao SAR, attended the event.

AIE Expo 2026 will take place from December 3 to 5 in Macao and Zhuhai, a city in south China's Guangdong Province. The event aims to serve as a platform for showcasing the latest achievements in China's intelligent manufacturing.

It is expected to attract more than 1,000 technology companies, feature over 20,000 products, and welcome 50,000 industry professionals from China and abroad. More than 100 new products and technologies are scheduled to make their global debuts.

The Zhuhai venue will focus on four industrial sectors, including manufacturing, mobility, living, and electronics, with an emphasis on supply chains and business matchmaking, while the Macao venue will feature four interactive experience zones and six exhibition zones, offering immersive demonstrations and displays of emerging technologies.

At the press conference, companies from Guangzhou, Zhuhai and other cities in the GBA presented innovations in smart healthcare, smart home technologies, cloud computing, and artificial intelligence (AI).

Chen Haibin, a representative of Guangzhou-based Gamsing Technology Co., Ltd., said that moving innovation from the laboratory to the production line requires bringing together cutting-edge technologies, a well-integrated supply chain and real market demand.

He noted that AIE Expo's approach, which combines frontier technology showcases in Macao with targeted business matchmaking in Zhuhai, could help bridge the gap between technological innovation and industrial application.

Confirmed exhibitors include HONOR, OPPO, TCL, Haier, Gree, Tesla, NIO, GAC International, EHang, Jaten Robotics, and XAG, spanning sectors such as intelligent manufacturing, smart mobility, smart living, next-generation electronics, embodied AI and computing hardware.
Professional buyers from Europe, the United States, the Middle East, Africa, and ASEAN have already registered to attend.
A series of business matchmaking sessions will help exhibitors connect with potential buyers across these key sectors.

Leveraging Macao's role as a platform for commercial and trade cooperation between China and Portuguese-speaking countries, the expo aims to deepen collaboration in technological innovation and industrial development between the two sides.
[continua sulla fonte originale]

items.title: Trump, Xi and Putin sit down for a rare 3-way meeting in China
text: President Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin sat down for a meeting in Shenzhen, China, on Thursday — a rare face-to-face encounter for the leaders of three of the world's most powerful countries.

All three made brief opening statements before meeting behind closed doors for about an hour and a half. The leaders did not offer joint or separate statements to reporters after the sit-down, and Mr. Trump immediately left for the airport to return home.

Putin's senior aid Yuri Ushakov told reporters after the meeting that the atmosphere had been good, and the Kremlin quickly released what it said was a statement jointly agreed on by all three leaders characterizing the talks.

The three men "exchanged views in detail on the current international situation and reaffirmed their commitment to maintaining strategic stability and international security," the Kremlin readout said, adding that as permanent members of the United Nations Security Council, they had "reaffirmed their commitment to reforming the UN so that it can more effectively respond to global challenges and fulfill its fundamental mission in the area of international peace and security."

They also committed to increasing gas and oil production "for the benefit of all countries," agreed on the "fundamental importance" of "the principle of state consent and respect for the immunities of state officials," and said the "International Criminal Court and other similar bodies should not abuse their powers."
Finally, the Russian government said the leaders had "reaffirmed that there can be no winners in a nuclear war, and that it should never be unleashed."
The White House did not offer an immediate readout of the meeting, but indicated that Mr. Trump might speak with reporters on Air Force One during the flight back to the U.S.

The Kremlin shared a short video on social media, via Russian state media, showing Xi accompanying Putin as they walked out of the meeting to Putin's waiting motorcade. Before they exit the building, Putin is seen shaking Xi's hand, thanking him for hosting the gathering and telling him, according to Russian state media, that nobody had expected it to go so well.
Before the meeting, Mr. Trump met separately with Putin on the sidelines of the Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, and then with Xi.
"We've had a great relationship for many years," Mr. Trump said, standing alongside his Russian counterpart. "I think a lot of wonderful things can come out of this, or at least start."
As Mr. Trump approached Putin for a handshake, he said, "Who is that?" before laughing and saying, "He's my friend."
Russia's TASS news agency said the war in Ukraine was the main topic discussed by the two leaders, and that Putin left the meeting in "an excellent mood."
After the trilateral talks, Putin told reporters that Ukraine and Europe were "not yet ready" to make the compromises necessary to resolve the war, according to Russian media.

items.title: First Thing: Trump, Xi and Putin hold historic trilateral meeting in China
text: The three leaders spoke about international peace and nuclear weapons as Trump called Putin a ‘friend’. Plus, yes, GTA VI is really finally here, and the critics have their verdict: masterpiece
Don’t already get First Thing in your inbox? Sign up here

Good morning. Donald Trump has met Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping at the Apec summit in Shenzhen, and said the three leaders were “really making history”. The trilateral meeting lasted roughly an hour and a half, according to Chinese state media. On arrival the US president described his Russian counterpart as “my friend”.

Putin told Xi and Trump that their countries shared “many converging interests” when it came to resolving conflicts, including the full-scale war in Ukraine, which the Russian president started in 2022.

Trump said the three countries were “uniquely positioned” to discuss nuclear weapons, while Xi said “every effort must be made to prevent nuclear war” and that nuclear weapons ⁠should be comprehensively prohibited and completely ⁠destroyed.

China released a readout of an earlier Trump-Xi meeting, with the tone being largely positive, but containing a warning on Taiwan and a call to strengthen communication on trade and AI. Trump has now departed from China.

What was unusual about China’s welcome to the Japanese delegation? Apec’s Chinese hosts went out of their way to give world leaders a warm welcome as they arrived in Shenzhen, with one exception. Japan’s prime minister, Sanae Takaichi, had to make do with a modest guard of honour and a welcome from a relatively junior Chinese government official.
The Guardian is live blogging the Apec summit. You can follow it here.

Positioned for one of the biggest IPOs in history, Anthropic set the share price for its debut on the US stock market at $83, above its earlier estimates. The firm is slated to begin trading on Thursday under the ticker symbol ANT, with its chief executive, Dario Amodei, and other cofounders ringing the bell to open the Nasdaq exchange. Graeme Wearden has the latest on our business live blog.

What is the latest warning on the environmental impact of AI? The world’s datacentres will create 70% more carbon emissions within the next four years as the US and China turn to fossil fuels to power their AI growth agendas, according to the world’s energy watchdog.

Who has been accused of spying in Silicon Valley? The US Department of Justice has accused a Russian national of spying on employees of a Silicon Valley technology and defense company in an alleged effort to gather intelligence for Russia. Igor D’iu had been indicted on multiple charges.

Why have four Maryland high school students sued after an AI error? Four current and former students at a Maryland high school have filed a lawsuit a year after armed police detained them, prompted by an AI alert that mistook a bag of Doritos for a gun, in an incident that left them “fearing for their lives”.

Trump meets Putin and Xi for trilateral US, Russia, China talks at APEC
text: United States President Donald Trump has met with his Chinese and Russian counterparts for highly anticipated trilateral talks at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit.

Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin met for a “family photo” before convening for talks on the sidelines of the summit in Shenzhen, China, on Thursday in an unprecedented gathering of the world’s three superpowers.
Opening the meeting, Xi said that it “has groundbreaking significance”.
“The world is at peace when great powers live in harmony,” Xi said, adding that the three countries “should work together to address global challenges”.
In a major statement, the Chinese leader also said “nuclear weapons should be comprehensively banned and thoroughly destroyed, building a nuclear-free world,” reported China’s Xinhua news agency.
In Trump’s opening remarks, the US president said the three countries were “uniquely positioned” to discuss nuclear weapons.
“Too often past leaders avoided talking to leaders they had disagreements with,” he said. “No peace ever forged by declining opportunities.”

Meanwhile, in his opening remarks, Putin made it clear that the war in Ukraine would be the focus of his conversation, before the three retreated into closed-door talks which lasted for about 55 minutes.

The talks between the leaders of the world’s largest nuclear powers were not likely to produce major agreements, analysts say, given deep differences over Ukraine, Iran, nuclear weapons and trade. But the meeting had unnerved smaller countries that feared their interests might be disregarded.
Ahead of the trilateral gathering, Trump held separate bilateral meetings with both Xi and Putin on Thursday.
The US president described Xi as a “friend” and said Washington and Beijing enjoyed a “special relationship”.

“As long as the two of us are in charge, I don’t think we’ll have a problem,” Trump said in opening remarks at his meeting with the Chinese leader. He also boasted that “no other countries can do what we can”.
Trump said the US has done “amazing” things in the past two years, since he returned to power, while praising China for many of its gains over several years.
Xi, meanwhile, said that he remained committed to working with Trump to steer ties between their countries on the “correct course”.
Relations between Beijing and Washington have been stable and improving, Xi said to Trump at the start of their third one-on-one meeting this year, which lasted for about an hour.
“We have established a new definition of a constructive China-US relationship of strategic stability, giving it new substance based on respect, fairness and reciprocity,” Xi said.

Ahead of the bilateral meeting, Trump said the Board of Trade that he and the Chinese president agreed to form at their Beijing summit in May has brought balance to the two countries’ relationship. He said the US and China had split their tariffs in a “fair way”.
Earlier in the day, during talks with Putin, Trump also called the Russian leader a “friend”.

text: Alibaba's Revenue Beats Estimates During China's AI Boom                               1 / 1    Alibaba's Revenue Beats Estimates During China's AI Boom           Luz Ding  Updated Thu, November 19, 2026 at 4:10 AM MST 4 min read                                    BABA                                (Bloomberg) -- Alibaba Group Holding Ltd. (BABA) posted a stronger-than-projected 10% rise in revenue, reflecting the company's pivotal role in providing computing and services to propel China's AI development boom.

Revenue grew to 271.52 billion yuan ($40.7 billion) in the September quarter, exceeding the average analyst estimate of 270.5 billion yuan. Net income more than tripled, in part because of gains from investments.

Alibaba faces growing pressure to show it can deliver on AI despite new limits on its access to data center chips. Washington this week moved to shut down a key loophole that Chinese hyperscalers like Alibaba use to access the advanced chips they need. That's turning investors more cautious on their growth potential, as well as their ability to train and run next-generation models. Alibaba's market value stands at roughly $200 billion, less than half its level just over a year ago when investors were betting on it to lead the industry.

It already ranks among the country's biggest AI spenders, plowing capital into research and data centers to drive a cloud service as well as development of cutting-edge AI models. The company benefits in part from renting cloud computing capacity to tech firms developing artificial intelligence, a business that's thrived alongside Chinese efforts to match US frontier players OpenAI and Anthropic PBC.

Chief Executive Officer Eddie Wu pledged more than $53 billion over a three-year period to build a full suite of services and businesses from models to chips. The company raised about $10.2 billion from a Hong Kong share sale in August, after Wu said spending would surpass original targets.

The company just upgraded its flagship large language model, the Qwen4-Max. The Qwen series is the world's most downloaded open weight model family. It offers a consumer-facing Qwen App, one of China's most popular, integrating functions including shopping, navigation, and travel booking, as well as a productivity tool dubbed Qwen Work. And it's Apple Inc.'s partner on AI services in China, set to roll out in December.

Wu in September said T-Head — the chipmaking arm recently approved for an IPO in Hong Kong — will soon roll out China's most powerful domestic semiconductors. It's shipped more than 560,000 units of its flagship Zhenwu chips so far. Wu said in September the latest Zhenwu V900, slated for mass production in early 2027, can power frontier-model training.
